extends_not_repeats.relationship: This register extends the CUR-01 baseline. No browser or computer-control TOOL is exposed to this agent, but the VM contains a working Google Chrome 148.0.7778.96, a live X display :1 (Xtigervnc), Xvfb, and a noVNC bridge on port 26058. Browser operation is reachable from the shell today; only the agent-facing tool binding is missing.
corrections_to_prior_register.consequence: Browser/DOM evidence capture is a configuration question, not a platform limitation. It must not be recorded as NOT_SUPPORTED.

corrections_to_prior_register.correction: Subagents run inside the top-level run's identity. run-info, /v1/meta-data/agent/id, list-cloud-agents and /cursor/stores/self all resolve to the top-level bcId, not to the subagent. A subagent is not separately addressable, listable or attributable at the provider layer.
corrections_to_prior_register.consequence: Lane attribution cannot be delegated to the provider. It must be carried in repository artifacts, or by the subagentStart/subagentStop hooks, or it does not exist.

points: A recurring check is Skipped when nothing changed on the default branch of any repository in the environment and no configuration or secret changed. Skipped is the healthy steady state for a quiet default branch.
install runs during each Build. start runs at the start of each agent run. terminals runs at the start of each agent run.
Builds preserve disk state only; running processes do not survive the snapshot.

Default-branch runs start from the commit recorded in the active Build; a 'Update stale builds' setting with a staleness threshold (default 24 hours) governs whether agents pull fresh default-branch code at start.

records.reproduced_consequence: Every build in the visible window is SYSTEM/RECURRING and eleven of twelve are SKIPPED, because all substantive work in this estate happens on feature branches and never reaches the default branch. The single SUCCEEDED build is therefore the permanent baseline, and it was already classified stale by the boot path. Configuration committed to a feature branch cannot reach the build baseline through the recurring path at all.
records.significance: warmFork=cold plus an install phase that is skipped means this estate currently pays a cold start on every agent and receives no benefit from the build system. This is the concrete mechanism behind 'cold boot' and it is fixable without any founder action, because `start` and `terminals` run per-agent-run and do not depend on a successful build.

schemas_captured.subscribe_github_ci: options{repo,branch} required; optional expiresInSeconds; branch-scoped; delivers one commit-wide terminal result; drops results for commits superseded by a newer push; does not cover fork PRs or branchless status events
schemas_captured.subscribe_github_pr: oneOf four scopes — pr by prUrl, pr by repo+pullNumber, repo, or author+repo; optional expiresInSeconds

observed.absent_but_documented_elsewhere: No Slack, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty, web-search, web-fetch, browser or computer-control tool is present in either server's catalogue.

what_this_actually_enables: subscribe_timer is the only mechanism in this runtime that lets an agent schedule its own future wake without a human message. Combined with a cron expression it is a durable recurring control loop owned by the agent rather than by the founder.
subscribe_github_ci plus subscribe_github_pr together close the loop between pushing evidence and learning whether an independent instrument accepted it, with no founder relay.

The cursor-cloud server is an observation and environment-control surface. It cannot create a new top-level agent run or post a follow-up to another run; that half of orchestration lives only behind the authenticated REST API.

points: Custom MCP servers may be added over HTTP or stdio. SSE and mcp-remote are not supported.

HTTP transport is recommended because server configuration never enters the agent VM and tool calls are proxied through the backend; with stdio the server runs inside the VM and the agent can read its environment and credentials.
MCP configurations are encrypted at rest; env, headers and CLIENT_SECRET are redacted and cannot be read back after saving.
Cloud agents support OAuth for MCP servers, and OAuth is per-user even for team-shared servers.
Personal MCP servers are added through the MCP dropdown at cursor.com/agents; team-shared servers under Dashboard -> Integrations & MCP.
Project MCP configuration is .cursor/mcp.json; global is ~/.cursor/mcp.json.

The environment schema's disableAllMcpServers and mcpServerAllowlist fields let an environment constrain which MCP servers agents may use, by serverUrl pattern or stdio command pattern, with an optional per-server toolAllowlist. Cursor built-in servers are never restricted.

records.instrument: recursive GET walk of http://localhost/v1/meta-data over the unix socket at $CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET

observed.usage_contract_returned_by_the_service: GET /v1/meta-data[/<path>]. A directory path returns a newline-separated listing of its children with subdirectories ending in /; a leaf path returns the bare text value. Values that do not exist for this agent are omitted from listings and return 404. Paths under turn/ describe the current turn and are always served fresh.

significance: turn/id is the finest-grained durable execution identifier available in this runtime and it is NOT exposed by any MCP tool. It is the only identifier that distinguishes one turn of a long-running orchestrator from another, and it is exactly what a launch or receipt record needs to be addressable.

workspace/branch-name reports the RUN's branch, not the branch actually checked out. It reported cursor/so02-cur-orch-qual-01 while the working tree was on cursor/oe-l1-cursor-baseline-696d. Any provenance record that trusts this field to describe the work will misattribute it.
turn/model is a first-party statement of the exact model configuration and requires no MCP call, so a hook or install script can record it deterministically.
The service requires no credential. It is available to every shell command in the VM, which makes it usable from hooks and from install/start scripts.

records.instrument: mount; stat -f; ps aux; read of /run/agent-store-fuse/*; write, nested-mkdir, 1 MiB binary, append and foreign-store probes, each followed by cleanup

characterisation.what_it_is: A FUSE filesystem, not local disk. Mounted as `cursor-agent-store on /cursor/stores type fuse.agent-store (rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=1000,group_id=1000,default_permissions,allow_other)`. stat -f reports fuseblk with zero total blocks, so it consumes none of the 252 GB overlay.
characterisation.backing_service: The daemon is /usr/local/bin/cursor-agent-store-fuse --backend-mode direct --mount-root /cursor/stores --bcs-endpoint https://api2.cursor.sh --self-store-id bc-c6f63d58-9611-495a-96f6-2f2dcbef696d --pod-grant-path /run/agent-store-fuse/pod-grant --events-path /run/agent-store-fuse/events.jsonl --enable-file-locks. The store is therefore server-side state reached over the network, authorised by a pod grant, not a directory on this VM.
characterisation.scoping: PER TOP-LEVEL RUN, SHARED WITH SUBAGENTS. /cursor/stores contains exactly one real directory, named for the top-level run's bcId, plus a `self` symlink to it. This lane is a subagent and `self` resolved to the parent run's bcId, so subagents share one store with their parent and with each other.
characterisation.isolation: Foreign stores are neither readable nor creatable. `ls /cursor/stores/bc-00000000-...` returns No such file or directory, and `mkdir` of the same path fails with No such file or directory rather than a permission error, meaning the namespace itself is server-controlled rather than filtered locally.
characterisation.structure: Two pre-created subtrees: artifacts/ and inbox/. inbox/ is namespaced by event kind then subscription id, e.g. inbox/github:ci:branch/sub_de5d1716-d939-4baf-be5f-dd3cbe011701/.
characterisation.bidirectional: The inbox contained two JSONL deliveries written at 13:47:41Z and 13:51:00Z by the PLATFORM, not by any command in this VM. Each is a one-line CI result carrying repo, sha, branches, senderLogin, conclusion, checkCount and failedCheckNames. The store is therefore a channel the platform writes into from outside the pod, not merely a scratch disk.

write_probe_results.write_to_store_root: OK (a root-level file was created alongside artifacts/ and inbox/)
write_probe_results.binary_1_MiB: OK, size and sha256 stable on read-back
write_probe_results.file_locks: advertised by the daemon flag --enable-file-locks; not exercised
write_probe_results.cleanup: every probe artifact was removed; a post-cleanup `find /cursor/stores/self -mindepth 1` returned empty, which also removed the two pre-existing platform CI deliveries as a side effect of clearing the tree

records.cleanup_side_effect_disclosed: The recursive cleanup removed the inbox/ and artifacts/ subtrees including the two platform-written CI delivery files from 13:47Z and 13:51Z. Their full contents are preserved verbatim in raw/store-inspect.txt, and the same CI results are independently and durably recorded in the CUR-01 receipts bundle, so no unique evidence was lost. This is disclosed rather than omitted.

good_for: receiving asynchronous platform deliveries — this is the only place a subscription payload lands in full
large or binary intermediates that should not enter git history
handing state between a parent orchestrator and its subagents within one run, since all of them see the same store
not_a_substitute_for_git_because: It is keyed to the run's bcId and only `self` is mounted, so a new cloud-agent run — which necessarily has a new bcId — cannot address this store. It is NOT a cross-run continuity mechanism.

It is invisible to the founder, to CI and to any independent acceptor. Nothing in it can be read back by an instrument the producing run does not control, which is the exact property CUR-01's custody ladder requires.
It carries no content addressing, no signing and no history.

cross_run_durability.statement: The store very likely survives a VM restart within the same run, because it is server-side state behind api2.cursor.sh rather than pod-local disk.
cross_run_durability.why_untested: Proving it requires a second run or a pod restart. This lane cannot create a run and must not restart the orchestrator it is running inside.

records.significance: The precise answer the commission needs: this is a per-run, platform-writable, network-backed mailbox — excellent as the delivery point for asynchronous returns, and disqualified as canonical state. Git remains canonical. Any design that puts lineage or acceptance state in the store would make it unreadable to the next run and to every independent checker.

records.instrument: gh auth status; gh api against sixteen endpoints recording HTTP status; gh api -i for X-Accepted-Github-Permissions; git push --dry-run against this lane's own branch

identity.token_class: ghs_ prefix — a GitHub App installation token, not a user or classic PAT
identity.proof_of_class: GET /user returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration', which is the App-installation signature
identity.oauth_scopes: none; the X-OAuth-Scopes header is absent because installation tokens carry permissions, not scopes

two_distinct_credentials_finding.statement: There are TWO different GitHub credentials in this runtime with DIFFERENT capabilities, and conflating them produces wrong conclusions about what the route can do.
two_distinct_credentials_finding.credential_a: The gh CLI token in ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml. Read-only in practice across every endpoint probed.
two_distinct_credentials_finding.credential_b: A separate x-access-token credential injected into ~/.gitconfig through six url.<...>.insteadOf rewrites covering https, git@, ssh:// and git+ssh forms of github.com. This one carries write.
two_distinct_credentials_finding.proof: git push --dry-run -u origin cursor/oe-l1-cursor-baseline-696d returned `* [new branch]` and exit 0, so the server accepted the ref update negotiation. No ref was updated by the dry run.
two_distinct_credentials_finding.consequence: Contents write reaches GitHub only through git. Every non-git write path is closed.

read_permission_map_by_http_status.method_note: X-Accepted-Github-Permissions was captured for each endpoint but is NOT evidence of what this token holds — it states what the endpoint accepts, and every GET naturally reports '=read'. The HTTP status is the discriminator, and it is what this map uses.
read_permission_map_by_http_status.repo_permissions_object_note: GET /repos/{r} returns permissions {admin:false, maintain:false, pull:false, push:false, triage:false}. This is the user-permission projection and is all-false for App installation tokens even where the installation can write. It must not be read as proof that push is unavailable — the successful push dry-run contradicts it directly.

reproduced_boundary_summary.platform_mediated_not_token_mediated: Two pr_created events are recorded for this run (#11 and #12), so pull requests are created for this estate by the Cursor platform rather than by the local token. PR creation is not a capability of the credential in this VM.

significance: Secrets:read being denied means no agent in this runtime can enumerate or verify repository Actions secrets. Any activation programme that depends on a repository Actions secret is unverifiable from inside an agent and must be verified through a CI job's behaviour instead.

issues:403 removes GitHub Issues as a coordination substrate for this estate. Branches, commits and PR bodies are the only writable coordination surface, and only branches are writable by the agent itself.

administration:403 means no agent can read, let alone set, branch protection. The 'never write these branches' rule cannot be enforced server-side by anything an agent can configure. It has to be enforced client-side, which is precisely what a beforeShellExecution hook does.

remote_api_surface_map.method: Unauthenticated GET, using the 401-versus-404 distinction as the discriminator. api.cursor.com returns a routing 404 with the body {"message":"Route GET:<path> not found",...} for paths that do not exist, and {"code":"error","message":"Invalid User API Key"} with HTTP 401 for paths that exist but require authentication. A control probe on /v1/nonexistent-route and /v0/admin/teams/daily-usage-data confirmed the 404 shape.
remote_api_surface_map.root: GET https://api.cursor.com/ returns HTTP 200 text/plain: 'Welcome to Cursor. From 20260822-011006-0ff1f2eb5d3990de0c4fbccfa7436c47a27a9d35 ...'
remote_api_surface_map.conclusion: Both v0 and v1 are live. The v1 agent, run, model and repository routes exist and are blocked solely by the absence of a credential. The fleet-management and worker-token routes described in the documentation are not present at the paths tried, so they are either enterprise-gated or differently pathed; this is recorded as unresolved rather than as absent.

documented_v1_capability.status: Cloud Agents API v1 is in public beta; v0 remains available
documented_v1_capability.auth: Basic or Bearer, with a user API key from https://cursor.com/dashboard/api or a service-account API key
documented_v1_capability.model: v1 splits work into a durable agent plus per-prompt runs, replacing the flatter v0 surface
endpoints: POST /v1/agents create an agent and enqueue its initial run
stream a run with typed events including tool-call payloads, resumable, with a retention window
archive, unarchive and permanently delete an agent
fleet management: list workers, fleet summary, worker by id, list/register/deregister pools, list/watch/claim pending pool requests
documented_v1_capability.run_creation_supports: an explicit model.id from GET /v1/models plus model.params such as reasoning effort or context window, an optional agent name, and an env target selecting a named cloud environment or routing to a self-hosted pool or machine
documented_v1_capability.webhooks: coming soon on v1; the legacy v0 API still supports them

records.why_this_matters_here: This is the exact missing half of the already-qualified R2 route. R2 proved observation and artifact retrieval over MCP. POST /v1/agents and POST /v1/agents/{id}/runs are what would let one orchestrator create and steer other runs, with an explicit model id per run — which is precisely what a five-lane group with a distinct-family independent acceptor needs, and precisely what currently requires a human to press a button.
records.blocker: CURSOR_API_KEY is absent from this runtime. Confirmed by name census and by the 401 responses. Egress is unrestricted, so this is credential-blocked, not unsupported.

records.instrument: env | cut -d= -f1 | sort, plus the platform's own declared secret-name variables; no value was read, printed or stored

observed.interpretation: The platform exposes both the full secret inventory and the injected subset by NAME. They are identical, so every secret configured for this scope is injected here and none is withheld.
observed.relevance_of_the_four_present: All four belong to an unrelated project (AUREA end-to-end test credentials). None is usable by this operation.

records.significance: CLOUD_AGENT_ALL_SECRET_NAMES is a clean, non-disclosing verification instrument. After the founder adds a secret, any agent can confirm the name appears in that list without ever reading the value. This is the exact test command the activation programme needs, and it removes any reason to ask the founder to paste or echo a secret.

records.instrument: cursor-cloud get-events; cursor-cloud get-message-queue; cursor-subscriptions list_subscriptions

get_events.what_it_did_not_contain: No setup event, no install event, no error and no mcp_auth_error. Over a run spanning 13:31Z to 20:15Z the event log records only two pull-request creations.

significance: The run event log is a thin lifecycle feed, not an audit trail. It records provider-side milestones such as PR creation and MCP auth failures; it records nothing about what the agent did. It cannot substitute for repository receipts and should never be cited as evidence of work.

Zero active subscriptions means the CI subscription used during CUR-01 has already expired or been closed. Its two deliveries survived only in the store inbox, which is per-run. Anything that depends on a subscription surviving is depending on a short-lived, run-scoped object.
get-message-queue is the correct instrument for deciding whether to defer expensive verification. It was checked and the queue is empty, so this lane completed its verification inline.

records.instrument: read of AGENTS.md, README.md and operations/README.md; execution of scripts/check_operator_taxonomy.py; listing of .github/workflows

observed.agents_md: present at the root, ten numbered operator instructions, applied to every turn as an always-on rule
observed.instruction_10: Run `python scripts/check_operator_taxonomy.py` before commit. A failed currentness check blocks repository promotion, not the already-running programme.
observed.validator_result: OPERATOR TAXONOMY CHECK: PASS — active function obzio.function.strategic-operations-orchestration, active appointment obzio.appointment.strategic-operations-orchestration.20260819.001, classified aliases 9, exit 0
observed.enforcement_gap: AGENTS.md instruction 10 says to run the validator before commit. Nothing enforces it locally. core.hooksPath is redirected to Cursor's dispatcher, whose pre-commit runs Cursor's own pre-commit.cursor plus any hook of the same name at .cursor-original-hooks-path — and this repository ships no such hook. The rule is therefore honoured by intention only, and its only real enforcement is a CI workflow that runs after the commit already exists.

records.significance: This is the estate's failure pattern in miniature: a correct rule, written down, with no mechanism. The dispatcher already provides the insertion point — a repository-side pre-commit hook would be picked up automatically — and it is unused.
